def-semi-explicit-index-one-dae-and-cons:
## Definition

Let $d,m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$ and $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$. A **semi-explicit differential-algebraic equation (DAE)** on $\Omega$ is

$$
x'(t)=f(t,x(t),z(t)),\qquad 0=g(t,x(t),z(t)).
$$

The $x$-coordinates are the **differential variables** because their derivatives occur in the first equation. The $z$-coordinates are the **algebraic variables** because their derivatives do not occur. A solution on an interval $I$ is a pair of functions $x:I\to\mathbb R^d$, $z:I\to\mathbb R^m$ whose graph lies in $\Omega$, with $x$ differentiable, satisfying both displayed equations at every $t\in I$. An initial pair $(x_0,z_0)$ at $t_0$ is **algebraically consistent** when $g(t_0,x_0,z_0)=0$. On the regular index-one branch below this is the algebraic initial condition used for reduction. For higher-index systems, algebraic consistency is only necessary: differentiated constraints may impose additional initial conditions.

At a point with $g(t_*,x_*,z_*)=0$, the presentation is **regular index one** when $f,g$ are $C^1$ near the point and the square Jacobian $g_z(t_*,x_*,z_*)=D_zg(t_*,x_*,z_*)$ is invertible. The [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]] then supplies a unique local branch $z=\psi(t,x)$ through that point. Only that selected branch is used in local numerical claims. Higher-index systems and points with singular $g_z$ are outside this index-one interface.
def-regular-differentiation-index:
## Definition

Fix a semi-explicit presentation $x'=f(t,x,z)$, $0=g(t,x,z)$ as in [[def-semi-explicit-index-one-dae-and-consistent-initial-data]] and a sufficiently differentiable consistent local solution. Differentiate the algebraic constraint along the differential equation, substituting $x'=f(t,x,z)$ and any previously obtained derivative relations at each stage. The **differentiation index in this convention** is the least positive integer $k$ for which the original constraint and its first $k$ differentiated equations locally determine $z$ and $z'$, with the equation for the highest derivative of $z$ having an invertible square Jacobian on a neighborhood of the solution. If no such finite $k$ exists, this local index is undefined. This convention counts through the first derivative of the algebraic variables and is local to the fixed presentation; it is not a universal index theory for arbitrary implicit systems.

If $g_z$ is invertible, one differentiation gives

$$
g_t+g_x f+g_z z'=0,
$$

which determines $z'$, so the index is one. If $g_z$ is singular, the index must be checked from the actual differentiated equations; no index-one conclusion follows from this definition alone.
thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-redu:
## Statement

Let $d,m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$, $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^k$ for $k\ge1$. Suppose $g(t_*,x_*,z_*)=0$ and $g_z(t_*,x_*,z_*)$ is invertible. Then there are neighborhoods $U$ of $(t_*,x_*)$ and $V$ of $z_*$, and a unique $C^k$ map $\psi:U\to V$, such that, for $(t,x)\in U$ and $z\in V$,

$$
g(t,x,z)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z=\psi(t,x).
$$

Its derivatives satisfy

$$
\psi_t=-g_z^{-1}g_t,\qquad \psi_x=-g_z^{-1}g_x,
$$

with the derivatives of $g$ evaluated at $(t,x,\psi(t,x))$. The reduced vector field $F(t,x)=f(t,x,\psi(t,x))$ is $C^k$ on $U$. Thus solutions of the DAE that stay in this selected chart are exactly solutions of $x'=F(t,x)$ paired with $z=\psi(t,x)$.
lem-index-one-dae-algebraic-residual-to-:
## Statement

Let $K$ be a compact set of base points $(t,x)$ in a selected branch chart from [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]], and put $z_*=\psi(t,x)$. Suppose $g(t,x,\cdot)$ is $C^2$ on $B(z_*,\rho)$ for every $(t,x)\in K$. Let $G_*(t,x)=g_z(t,x,\psi(t,x))$. Assume common constants $\gamma>0$, $\Lambda\ge0$, and $\rho>0$ satisfy

$$
\|G_*(t,x)v\|_2\ge\gamma\|v\|_2\quad(v\in\mathbb R^m),\qquad \|g_z(t,x,z)-G_*(t,x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\Lambda\|z-\psi(t,x)\|_2
$$

for every $(t,x)\in K$ and $z\in B(\psi(t,x),\rho)$; if $\Lambda>0$, assume $\rho\le\gamma/(\sqrt m\,\Lambda)$. Then, uniformly for all such base points and candidates,

$$
\|z-z_*\|_2\le \frac{2}{\gamma}\|g(t,x,z)\|_2.
$$

The estimate is local: it applies only to candidates in the specified branch ball and does not turn a residual into a global branch or uniqueness certificate.
alg-index-one-dae-consistent-initializat:
## Definition

Let $f,g$ define a regular index-one DAE and let $U\times V$ be a selected local branch chart from [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]], so $g(t,x,z)=0$ is equivalent to $z=\psi(t,x)$ there. Input $t_0,x_0$, a seed $z_{\mathrm{seed}}\in V$, an algebraic residual tolerance $\varepsilon_a\ge0$, and a finite Newton-correction budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$. If $(t_0,x_0)\notin U$, $g(t_0,x_0,\cdot)$ is undefined at the seed, or dimensions do not match, return invalid-input.

Call [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on the square residual $G(z)=g(t_0,x_0,z)$, with initial value $z_{\mathrm{seed}}$, tolerance $\varepsilon_a$, and budget $N$, restricting evaluations to the chart's open $z$-domain. If it reports root, reevaluate $G(z_0)$ once: if that residual is exactly zero, return $(x_0,z_0,\texttt{exact-consistent})$; otherwise return $(x_0,z_0,\texttt{approximate-consistent})$ and its norm. Map singular-jacobian, invalid-trial, and iteration-budget-exhausted to the corresponding initialization statuses and return the last valid iterate.

The procedure makes no arbitrary-start convergence claim. approximate-consistent records a residual bound; it is not relabeled as exact consistency. Under the index-one branch hypotheses an exact consistent value exists locally, by [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]], but the finite Newton budget may fail to find it.

The solve has $m$ algebraic unknowns. With budget $N$, the Newton supplier performs at most $N$ corrections, each using one $m\times m$ Jacobian solve, and at most $N+1$ residual evaluations. A root status adds one residual reevaluation for recording, so the procedure uses at most $N+2$ residual evaluations. Residual/Jacobian assembly and linear-solve costs depend on the chosen backend.
alg-index-one-dae-backward-euler-stepper:
## Definition

Input $f,g$, a constant grid $t_n=t_0+nh$ with $h>0$ and $N_t\in\mathbb N$, an initial pair $(X_0,Z_0)$, and a selected open tube inside the local branch chart of [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]], where $g(t,x,z)=0$ is equivalent to $z=\psi(t,x)$. Also input positive residual tolerances $\eta_d,\eta_a$, a finite Newton-correction budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, and an initial algebraic-residual bound $\eta_{a,0}\ge0$. Return invalid-grid if $h\le0$ or $N_t=0$, invalid-input for incompatible dimensions or data outside the function domains, and inconsistent-initial-data if $\|g(t_0,X_0,Z_0)\|_2>\eta_{a,0}$.

For $n=1,\ldots,N_t$, form the coupled update residual

$$
R_n(X,Z)=\bigl(X-X_{n-1}-h f(t_n,X,Z),\ g(t_n,X,Z)\bigr)
$$

and the scaled square residual

$$
\mathcal R_n(X,Z)=\left(\frac{X-X_{n-1}-h f(t_n,X,Z)}{h\eta_d},\ \frac{g(t_n,X,Z)}{\eta_a}\right).
$$

Use $(X_{n-1},Z_{n-1})$ as the Newton seed, and call [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on $\mathcal R_n$ with residual tolerance $1$, budget $B$, and the selected tube as its evaluation domain. If the returned status is root and the candidate lies in the selected tube, reevaluate $R_n$ once to retain both unscaled residuals, then append the candidate. Otherwise return the corresponding singular-Jacobian, invalid-trial, or iteration-budget-exhausted status and the already computed prefix. The input functions are defined on the selected tube, so no separate evaluation-failure branch is needed. If every step is accepted, return completed and the state sequence.

An accepted step satisfies $\|r^d_n\|_2\le\eta_d$ for the derivative residual $r^d_n=(X_n-X_{n-1})/h-f(t_n,X_n,Z_n)$, and $\|r^a_n\|_2\le\eta_a$ for the algebraic residual $r^a_n=g(t_n,X_n,Z_n)$. This follows because each block norm is at most the norm of their concatenation. root means only that the scaled residual tolerance was met; it does not assert an exact zero, uniqueness, Newton convergence from an arbitrary seed, or a discretization error bound.

Each step solves a coupled block system with $d+m$ unknowns. At most $B$ Newton corrections and $B+1$ Newton residual evaluations are made per attempted step, plus at most one residual reevaluation to record the unscaled blocks after a root status. Each correction uses one solve with the current $(d+m)$-dimensional block Jacobian. Work per residual, Jacobian assembly, and linear solve depends on the backend.
alg-index-one-dae-bdf2-stepper:
## Definition

Input $f,g$, a constant grid $t_n=t_0+nh$ with $h>0$ and $N_t\ge2$, two starting pairs $(X_0,Z_0),(X_1,Z_1)$, and a selected open tube inside the local branch chart of [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]], where $g(t,x,z)=0$ is equivalent to $z=\psi(t,x)$. Also input positive residual tolerances $\eta_d,\eta_a$ and a finite Newton-correction budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$. Each starting algebraic residual must meet its supplied bound; otherwise return inconsistent-initial-data. Return invalid-grid for a nonpositive step or fewer than two starting states, and invalid-input for incompatible dimensions or data outside the function domains.

For $n=2,\ldots,N_t$, form

$$
R_n(X,Z)=\bigl(3X-4X_{n-1}+X_{n-2}-2h f(t_n,X,Z),\ g(t_n,X,Z)\bigr)
$$

and

$$
\mathcal R_n(X,Z)=\left(\frac{3X-4X_{n-1}+X_{n-2}-2h f(t_n,X,Z)}{2h\eta_d},\ \frac{g(t_n,X,Z)}{\eta_a}\right).
$$

Use $(2X_{n-1}-X_{n-2},Z_{n-1})$ as the Newton seed and call [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on $\mathcal R_n$ with tolerance $1$, budget $B$, and the selected tube as the evaluation domain. Append a candidate only when Newton reports root and the candidate lies in the tube; reevaluate $R_n$ once to record its unscaled residual blocks. Otherwise return the corresponding singular-Jacobian, invalid-trial, or iteration-budget-exhausted status with the computed prefix. The input functions are defined on the selected tube, so no separate evaluation-failure branch is needed. If all steps are accepted, return completed.

For an accepted step, the constant-step BDF2 derivative residual is
$$
r^d_n=\frac{3X_n-4X_{n-1}+X_{n-2}}{2h}-f(t_n,X_n,Z_n),
$$
and the algebraic residual is $r^a_n=g(t_n,X_n,Z_n)$. The scaling ensures $\|r^d_n\|_2\le\eta_d$ and $\|r^a_n\|_2\le\eta_a$. The procedure makes no claim that Newton finds a root or that an accepted state is the exact selected branch root.

Each step solves a coupled block system with $d+m$ unknowns. At most $B$ Newton corrections and $B+1$ Newton residual evaluations are made per attempted step, plus at most one residual reevaluation to record the unscaled blocks after a root status. Each correction uses one solve with the current $(d+m)$-dimensional block Jacobian. Work per residual, Jacobian assembly, and linear solve depends on the backend.
lem-index-one-dae-backward-euler-local-b:
## Statement

Let a compact exact solution segment lie in a common index-one branch chart with $f,g\in C^1$ and $g_z$ invertible on the graph. For each point $(t,x,\psi(t,x))$ on that segment, the coupled backward-Euler root equations

$$
X-\xi-hf(t,X,Z)=0,\qquad g(t,X,Z)=0
$$

have a unique root $(X,Z)$ in a selected neighborhood of $(x,\psi(t,x))$ whenever the step data $(h,t,\xi)$ are sufficiently close to $(0,t,x)$. On a compact subsegment contained in one chart with positive margin, the neighborhoods and a positive step bound can be chosen uniformly after restricting the input states to that neighborhood.
lem-index-one-dae-bdf2-local-branch:
## Statement

Let a compact exact solution segment lie in a common index-one branch chart with $f,g\in C^1$ and $g_z$ invertible on the graph. For each point $(t,x,\psi(t,x))$, the coupled constant-step BDF2 root equations

$$
3X-4\xi+\zeta-2hf(t,X,Z)=0,\qquad g(t,X,Z)=0
$$

have a unique root $(X,Z)$ in a selected neighborhood of $(x,\psi(t,x))$ whenever $(h,t,\xi,\zeta)$ is sufficiently close to $(0,t,x,x)$. On a compact subsegment in one chart with positive margin, one may choose a common positive step bound after restricting the two input states to neighborhoods of the reference graph.
thm-index-one-dae-finite-budget-solvers-:
## Statement

Suppose the initialization and stepper algorithms in [[alg-index-one-dae-consistent-initialization]], [[alg-index-one-dae-backward-euler-stepper]], and [[alg-index-one-dae-bdf2-stepper]] are run with finite grid length and finite Newton budget $B$. Each call returns a status after finitely many residual evaluations. A Newton call makes at most $B+1$ residual evaluations. Initialization and a time-step wrapper may each make one additional residual evaluation after a root status to record the returned residual norm or unscaled blocks, so initialization uses at most $B+2$ evaluations and a stepper with $S$ attempted steps uses at most $S(B+2)$ evaluations before returning a failure status or completed. This is a termination statement only; it does not assert that any residual tolerance is attained.
thm-index-one-dae-backward-euler-first-o:
## Statement

For the semi-explicit DAE with $x\in\mathbb R^d$, $z\in\mathbb R^m$, and $d,m\ge1$, let $x'=F(t,x)$ be the reduced ODE from [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]] on $[0,T]$, with exact solution $\bar x\in C^2$. Suppose all exact and numerical states lie in a common compact branch tube, $F$ is Lipschitz in $x$ there with constant $L$, $\psi$ is Lipschitz in $x$ with constant $L_\psi$, and $f$ is Lipschitz in $z$ with constant $L_z$. Assume the residual lemma's hypotheses hold uniformly on this tube: there are common $\gamma>0$, $\Lambda\ge0$, and $\rho>0$ for its lower singular-value and Jacobian-Lipschitz bounds at every base point, with $\rho\le\gamma/(\sqrt m\,\Lambda)$ when $\Lambda>0$; all numerical algebraic candidates lie in the corresponding balls $B(\psi(t_n,X_n),\rho)$. Use a uniform grid $t_n=nh$, $h=T/N$, $T>0$, and $N\ge1$. Assume the starting pair also lies in its branch ball and

$$
\|X_0-\bar x(0)\|_2\le C_0h,\qquad \|g(0,X_0,Z_0)\|_2\le C_{a,0}h.
$$

For each $1\le n\le N$, suppose $(X_n,Z_n)$ lies in the branch ball and its coupled backward-Euler residuals satisfy

$$
r^d_n=\frac{X_n-X_{n-1}}h-f(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad r^a_n=g(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad \|r^d_n\|_2\le C_dh,\quad \|r^a_n\|_2\le C_ah.
$$

Then a constant $C$, independent of $h$, satisfies

$$
\max_{0\le n\le N}\Bigl(\|X_n-\bar x(t_n)\|_2+\|Z_n-\psi(t_n,\bar x(t_n))\|_2\Bigr)\le Ch
$$

for all sufficiently small $h$. This is a conditional accuracy result for accepted residuals; the finite-budget solver may return a failure status.
thm-index-one-dae-bdf2-second-order-with:
## Statement

For the semi-explicit DAE with $x\in\mathbb R^d$, $z\in\mathbb R^m$, and $d,m\ge1$, let $x'=F(t,x)$ be the reduced ODE from [[thm-index-one-dae-implicit-function-reduction]] on $[0,T]$, with exact solution $\bar x\in C^3$. Assume $F$ is Lipschitz in $x$ on a common compact tube with constant $L$, $\psi$ is Lipschitz in $x$ there with constant $L_\psi$, $f$ is Lipschitz in $z$ with constant $L_z$, and the residual lemma's hypotheses hold uniformly on this tube: common $\gamma>0$, $\Lambda\ge0$, and $\rho>0$ in its lower singular-value and Jacobian-Lipschitz bounds, with $\rho\le\gamma/(\sqrt m\,\Lambda)$ when $\Lambda>0$. Every numerical algebraic candidate lies in its corresponding branch ball. Use a constant grid $t_n=nh$, $h=T/N$, $T>0$, and $N\ge2$. Suppose the two starting pairs satisfy

$$
\|X_j-\bar x(t_j)\|_2\le C_sh^2,\qquad \|g(t_j,X_j,Z_j)\|_2\le C_{a,s}h^2,\qquad j=0,1.
$$

For each $2\le n\le N$, suppose the constant-step BDF2 derivative and algebraic residuals satisfy

$$
r^d_n=\frac{3X_n-4X_{n-1}+X_{n-2}}{2h}-f(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad r^a_n=g(t_n,X_n,Z_n),\quad \|r^d_n\|_2\le C_dh^2,\quad \|r^a_n\|_2\le C_ah^2.
$$

Then, for all sufficiently small $h$, a constant $C$ independent of $h$ satisfies

$$
\max_{0\le n\le N}\Bigl(\|X_n-\bar x(t_n)\|_2+\|Z_n-\psi(t_n,\bar x(t_n))\|_2\Bigr)\le Ch^2.
$$

The starter hypothesis holds, in particular, for an exact consistent $X_0,Z_0$ and one backward-Euler startup from $X_0$ with derivative residual $O(h)$ and algebraic residual $O(h^2)$. The error theorem is conditional on the residual bounds and selected branch; it does not assert that a finite Newton budget meets them.
